predecessors.note: The Zhao core: Cliopatria's 208 'Dai' shape (the rebel Zhao of Zhao Xie) lies 88 of 142 cells inside this shape. Zhang Er page: 'the Kingdom of Zhao was split into two'.

land.text: the Kingdom of Changshan: 'central Hebei' (Eighteen Kingdoms table), carved out of the former Kingdom of Zhao

successors.note: Chen Yu took Changshan in 205 and restored Zhao under Zhao Xie (the dai dossier carries the Zhao line); Han Xin conquered it in October 205.

capitals.name: Xiangguo (Xingtai)
capitals.note: Not on any page opened: the Zhang Er page names no capital and the Jingxing page names Xiangguo only as the place where Zhao Xie was killed. Xiangguo is the traditional seat of Zhang Er; unverified. Coordinates are modern Xingtai.

rulers.name: Zhang Er
rulers.title: King of Changshan
rulers.note: Given Changshan by Xiang Yu in 206 BC (the infobox says 207-205); Chen Yu drove him out in 205 and he 'went to Hàn'; King of Zhao as a Han vassal from 204 or 203; died in the 7th month of the 5th year of Liu Bang's reign, c. September 202.

correction.text: the Kingdom of Changshan: 'central Hebei' (Eighteen Kingdoms table), carved out of the former Kingdom of Zhao

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged (34,632 km2; 190 grid cells, 99 percent of them in Hebei) and it agrees with the table's 'central Hebei'; the page gives no area. The years change: the kingdom held 206-205, not to 204: 'In 205 BCE, Changshan was destroyed, and Zhao was restored with Zhao Xie as King of Zhao' (footnote) and 'In 205 BCE, Chen Yu... attacked Changshan' (Zhang Er page). In 205 the land is drawn in the dai dossier's new keyframe dai_-205.

region.text: the Kingdom of Changshan: 'central Hebei' (Eighteen Kingdoms table), carved out of the former Kingdom of Zhao

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu makes Zhang Er King of Changshan. Zhang Er page: given 'the Kingdom of Changshan (常山), which was given to Zhang Er' by Xiang Yu in 206 BC, when 'the Kingdom of Zhao was split into two'; Eighteen Kingdoms table: 'central Hebei', Zhang Er, Zhao's vice chancellor. The region is Cliopatria's shape; no boundary is named.

region.text: the Kingdom of Changshan: 'central Hebei' (Eighteen Kingdoms table), carved out of the former Kingdom of Zhao

ledger.note: 205: Chen Yu drives out Zhang Er. 'In 205 BCE, Chen Yu, believing that his merit was equal to that of Zhang Er' attacked Changshan with Tian Rong's force and restored Zhao; Zhang Er 'went to Hàn instead'. Eighteen Kingdoms footnote: 'In 205 BCE, Changshan was destroyed'. The Timeline page dates Chen Yu's conquest of Changshan 206.

region.text: the Kingdom of Changshan: 'central Hebei' (Eighteen Kingdoms table), carved out of the former Kingdom of Zhao

ledger.note: 205: the Kingdom of Changshan ends. Zhao is restored with Zhao Xie as king; Zhang Er is later made King of Zhao by Liu Bang (204 on the Timeline page, 203 on the Zhang Er page), a different kingdom.

wars.name: Chen Yu's seizure of Changshan

zones.text: the Kingdom of Changshan: 'central Hebei' (Eighteen Kingdoms table), carved out of the former Kingdom of Zhao

wars.outcome: Chen Yu, helped by Qi, defeated Zhang Er and restored Zhao; Zhang Er fled to Liu Bang and returned with Han Xin to destroy Chen Yu and Zhao Xie.
wars.note: The Timeline page: 'Rebellion in Zhao: Chen Yu conquers the Kingdom of Changshan. Zhang Er, the King of Changshan, takes shelter under Liu Bang', under 206.

certainty.note: 'Central Hebei' is all the pages say of the kingdom's land.

notes: Cliopatria's single Chang-shan shape (206-204) is cut to 206-205: the kingdom was destroyed in 205 (Eighteen Kingdoms footnote, Zhang Er page, Chu-Han Contention) or 206 (Timeline); 205 used, and Han Xin's conquest of the restored Zhao came in October 205. Not on any page: the capital (Xiangguo is from tradition, flagged), the boundary, an area, the month of Chen Yu's attack. Zhang Er's later Han-vassal Kingdom of Zhao (204 or 203 to his death in 202, then his son Zhang Ao) has no dossier: counterparts_needing_dossiers. The Zhang Er page's infobox gives his tenure as 207-205, which conflicts with its own text (206); 206 used. Pages beyond the hubs (Eighteen Kingdoms, Timeline, Chu-Han Contention): Zhang Er (Eighteen Kingdoms) only, within the budget; the Battle of Jingxing page (opened for dai) was used in notes only. Failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Er (a different person) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Er_(Han_dynasty) (not found). Gazetteer: no new names.
